citation: Cohen, Malloy and Nguyen (2020), Lazy Prices, Journal of Finance 75(3), 1371-1415; read as NBER WP 25084 (rev. March 2019)
feature: Similarity of a filing to the same firm's comparable filing a year earlier (cosine, Jaccard, edit distance, diff)
outcome: Stock returns; operating income, net income and sales; next SUE; bankruptcy
horizon: Returns: 3-month holding period from the month after filing, drift to 6 months and beyond; fundamentals 2 quarters ahead; bankruptcy within 1 year
incremental_to: Market, size, value, momentum and liquidity factors; size, book-to-market, past returns, SUE; dictionary tone change; document length
pit_handling: Signal dated by public filing date and traded from the following month; no pretrained model; delisting returns not stated; post-publication decay untested
informs_decision: Unit of analysis (document pairs); pairing rule (year-over-year versus consecutive quarters); similarity baseline for any narrative-change feature; text source (10-K and 10-Q)

citation: Bozanic, Roulstone and Van Buskirk (2018), Management earnings forecasts and other forward-looking statements, Journal of Accounting and Economics 65(1), 1-20; read as working paper of May 2015
text_source: Earnings press releases on 8-K (Results of Operations), EDGAR, 2004-2014; 67,276 announcements
feature: Share of forward-looking sentences, split into quantitative earnings statements (forecast-like) and all others
method: Keyword rules at sentence level; OLS; probit validation against I/B/E/S Guidance; seemingly unrelated regressions
outcome: Absolute announcement return; change in analyst forecast error for next quarter; disclosure mix under uncertainty
horizon: 3-day window; analyst forecasts within 7 days after the announcement
incremental_to: Magnitude of earnings surprise, earnings volatility, loss, size, book-to-market, return volatility; lagged disclosure share
pit_handling: Not addressed; rule-based with no trained model; sample requires analyst coverage and a prior-quarter 8-K
informs_decision: Text source (press release); benchmark coverage (numeric EPS guidance in about a third of covered firm-quarters); qualitative stratum; numeric-anchor rule; keyword rule baseline

citation: Tang, Yao and Zarowin (2025), Once Is Not Enough: An Analysis of Management Updates of Annual Earnings Forecasts, Journal of Accounting, Auditing & Finance (online), DOI 10.1177/0148558X251394474; read as working paper of May 2015
text_source: None (structured records from First Call Company Issued Guidance, annual EPS forecasts, fiscal years 1996-2011)
feature: Incidence, range width, midpoint and direction of updates to annual EPS guidance
method: Descriptive tabulation by update position; logit for updating; OLS of analyst revisions on forecast news
outcome: Whether and how guidance is updated; analyst consensus revision
horizon: Within the fiscal year; analyst forecasts from 90 days before to 30 days after each forecast
incremental_to: Concurrent earnings news, prior forecast error, reputation, news magnitude, loss, book-to-market, horizon, width, year and industry effects
pit_handling: Not addressed; no model; forecast bias is measured against realised earnings (hindsight by construction) but the direction tabulation needs none
informs_decision: First benchmark (guidance revision): prevalence of updates, class base rates, stratification by updating routine, treatment of reaffirmations and narrowed ranges

citation: Loughran and McDonald (2011), When Is a Liability Not a Liability? Textual Analysis, Dictionaries, and 10-Ks, Journal of Finance 66(1), 35-65
text_source: 10-K full text and MD&A, EDGAR, 1994-2008; 50,115 filings
feature: Share of negative, positive, uncertainty, litigious and modal words (finance lists versus Harvard list), raw and tf.idf weighted
outcome: Filing-period excess return; abnormal volume; later return volatility; earnings surprise; fraud suits; material weakness
horizon: Days 0-3; 252 days for volatility; next quarter for surprise; 12 to 18 months for events; 12 months for the portfolio
incremental_to: Size, book-to-market, share turnover, pre-filing alpha, institutional ownership, NASDAQ indicator, 48 industries
pit_handling: Word lists compiled by judgement from the same 1994-2008 filings used in the tests; sample requires trading in the year after filing; no pretrained model
informs_decision: Tone deferred; dictionary baseline for any later tone or confidence task; lexical baseline for hard-event association

citation: Chen, Matsumoto and Rajgopal (2011), Is silence golden? An empirical analysis of firms that stop giving quarterly earnings guidance, Journal of Accounting and Economics 51(1-2), 134-150; published abstract checked, October 2006 preprint also read
text_source: Press releases and conference call transcripts searched for stop announcements (per the preprint)
feature: Stopping quarterly earnings guidance, by public announcement or quietly
method: Event study with control firms; determinants model
outcome: Announcement return; analyst forecast dispersion and accuracy; return volatility; analyst following
informs_decision: Change classes: separate an announced withdrawal from guidance that is no longer mentioned; temporary suspensions and quarterly-to-annual switches need their own rules

citation: Hirst, Koonce and Venkataraman (2008), Management Earnings Forecasts: A Review and Framework, Accounting Horizons 22(3), 315-338, DOI 10.2308/acch.2008.22.3.315
feature: Management earnings forecasts: antecedents, characteristics, consequences
informs_decision: First benchmark: forecast characteristics are the least understood part and forecasting is iterative, which supports comparing consecutive forecasts

citation: Hassan, Hollander, van Lent and Tahoun (2019), Firm-Level Political Risk: Measurement and Effects, Quarterly Journal of Economics 134(4), 2135-2202; abstract read on the NBER WP 24029 page
feature: Share of the call devoted to political risk
method: Text-share measure from computational linguistics; panel regressions
outcome: Hiring, investment, lobbying and political donations; stock return volatility
horizon: Not given in the abstract (lobbying responds in the following quarter)
incremental_to: Sector-by-time effects; news about the mean of political shocks
informs_decision: Text source: a documented text feature that needs call transcripts, the deferred second layer

citation: Matsumoto, Pronk and Roelofsen (2011), What Makes Conference Calls Useful? The Information Content of Managers' Presentations and Analysts' Discussion Sessions, The Accounting Review 86(4), 1383-1414
text_source: More than 10,000 earnings conference call transcripts
feature: Presentation segment versus analyst discussion segment
outcome: Information each call segment adds to the earnings press release
informs_decision: Text source: calls add information beyond the press release, most in the question-and-answer part and when performance is poor

citation: Gow, Larcker and Zakolyukina (2021), Non-Answers During Conference Calls, Journal of Accounting Research 59(4), 1349-1384
feature: Whether a manager's response to an analyst question is a non-answer
method: Linguistic classification at the response level
outcome: Incidence of non-answers (about 11% of questions) and their determinants
informs_decision: Deferred tasks: a response-level label defined on transcripts; not usable on press releases

citation: Rogers and Van Buskirk (2013), Bundled forecasts in empirical accounting research, Journal of Accounting and Economics 55(1), 43-65
feature: Management earnings forecasts issued with the earnings announcement (bundled)
method: Measurement study; conditional expectations for forecast news
outcome: News content of a bundled forecast
informs_decision: Text source and endpoints: bundled forecasts are the most common kind, so guidance news is confounded with the earnings surprise unless conditioned on it

citation: Hutton, Miller and Skinner (2003), The Role of Supplementary Statements with Management Earnings Forecasts, Journal of Accounting Research 41(5), 867-890
feature: Supplementary statements: qualitative soft talk versus verifiable forward-looking statements
method: Classification of statements; market reaction tests
outcome: Stock price reaction to good-news and bad-news forecasts
informs_decision: Numeric-anchor rule and qualitative stratum: bad-news forecasts are informative alone; good-news forecasts only with verifiable supporting statements

citation: Davis, Piger and Sedor (2012), Beyond the Numbers: Measuring the Information Content of Earnings Press Release Language, Contemporary Accounting Research 29(3), 845-868, DOI 10.1111/j.1911-3846.2011.01130.x
feature: Net optimistic language (optimistic minus pessimistic word counts)
method: Word counts from linguistic categories; regressions
outcome: Future return on assets; market response around the announcement
horizon: Future ROA (horizon not given in the abstract); short announcement window
incremental_to: Earnings surprise and other quantifiable concurrent disclosures
informs_decision: Text source and tone: press-release language carries information beyond the numbers, so deferring tone is a labelling choice and not evidence of no signal
